title: [Frameit] The keyword and title sometimes have a vertical offset
body:
### New Issue Checklist - [x] Updated fastlane to the latest version - [x] I read the [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I read [docs.fastlane.tools](https://docs.fastlane.tools) - [x] I searched for [existing GitHub issues](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/issues) ### Issue Description I use Frameit with pleasure to frame my screenshots and add a localised keyword and title to it. The majority of text is aligned correctly: ![iphone5s-03_keyboarddiscovered-589996837d813aace56d9a0cf7b764a0_framed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2139844/30935231-52fefd12-a3d0-11e7-9cba-b786f8fc268f.png) Some of the framed screenshots show a vertical offset between the keyword and title. The offset might be a few pixels: ![iphone5s-02_smarttab-589996837d813aace56d9a0cf7b764a0_framed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2139844/30935245-62b46080-a3d0-11e7-89e6-2a3233ddd49b.png) Or massive: ![iphone5s-01_remotetab-589996837d813aace56d9a0cf7b764a0_framed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2139844/30935287-7a33d628-a3d0-11e7-8223-5e31a7bda185.png) My Framefile: ```json { "default": { "keyword": { "font": "./fonts/SF-UI-Display-Semibold.otf", "color": "#007AFF" }, "title": { "font": "./fonts/SF-UI-Display-Regular.otf", "color": "#002955" }, "background": "background.png", "padding": 25, "show_complete_frame": true, "stack_title" : false }, "data": [ { "filter": "01" }, { "filter": "02" }, { "filter": "03" }, { "filter": "04" }, { "filter": "05" } ] } ``` These are French, but I have got it in other languages too. The ones with a small offset, have a special character in either the keyword or title. For example in German the "ä", but also the apostrophe (') in a Dutch word. But I can't explain the massive offset in the example above, where no special character is used. The behaviour seems somehow random. Here are the *.strings files for the above French screenshots: _keyword.strings_ ```strings "01" = "Familier"; "02" = "Logos"; "03" = "Pratique"; "04" = "Glisser"; "05" = "Sélection directe"; ``` _title.strings_ ```strings "01" = "en apparence"; "02" = "pour changer de chaîne"; "03" = "pour entrer du texte"; "04" = "pour contrôler"; "05" = "des sources"; ``` Can you please investigate? ### Environment
